text:
incident-bot: P1 alert — elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate for model:redwood/s-1. Canary rollout flagged 15m ago. Error ratio 18% over 5m, threshold 5%. Paging on-call now. https://internal.status/INC-2026-044 :rotating_light:
Arjun K: I'm on it, looking at canary vs baseline. Any customer-facing errors?
Maya S: Support reports 3 customers seeing timeouts/duplicate tokens, one internal end-to-end test failed.
Leo T: Adding logs from canary tasks, quick grep shows `BrokenPipeError` in transformer loop for some requests. Pasting tail:```
2026-02-18T01:23:12.345Z INFO request_id=abc model=redwood/s-1 canary=true latency=123ms
2026-02-18T01:23:12.678Z ERROR request_id=abc model=redwood/s-1 canary=true exception=BrokenPipeError('write failed')
2026-02-18T01:23:12.679Z ERROR request_id=def model=redwood/s-1 canary=true exception=ValueError('Invalid tokenizer state')
```
Priya N: Interesting — baseline instances don't show Tokenizer errors. Could be a packaging mismatch or quantization kernel change in this canary build.
Rachel (ops): Customer impact: three high-usage tenants, cumulative failed requests ~2.4k in last 10m, some 95th latency spikes to 3.2s. Notified CS to open incidents with customers.
oncall-sre: @Arjun K please confirm whether to pause canary autoscaling or stop traffic to canary.
Arjun K: Temporarily cut traffic to canary via routing rule, setting weight to 0. Doing now.
deploy-bot: Routing update applied by arjunk — canary weight 0 -> effective in 12s.
Maya S: After cutting traffic, error rate dropped on prod edge. Still seeing failures reported from some cached requests — likely queued inflight.
Leo T: Timeline so far:
- T0 (1769923000): Canary rollout started (version s-1.12-canary)
- T0+5m: First spike detected by canary monitors
- T0+8m: incident-bot paged on-call
- T0+12m: Traffic routed away from canary
Arjun K: Hypotheses list: 1) Tokenizer binary mismatch (packaging) 2) Quantization-induced decode race 3) Kernel fallback path in new runtime triggers BrokenPipe on heavy concurrency
Priya N: I pulled the container diff between s-1.11 (stable) and s-1.12-canary. Notable changes: updated sentencepiece v0.2.95 -> v0.3.0, runtime patch enabling fused_kv_cache. Diff snippet:```diff
- sentencepiece==0.2.95
+ sentencepiece==0.3.0
+ fused_kv_cache=enabled
```
Rachel (ops): Can we check whether pinned model version for Dedicated customers was respected? Need to ensure no leakage.
Maya S: Confirming: Dedicated tenant configs show `model_pin: s-1.11` for all affected customers. They shouldn't have hit canary, so there may be routing mis-tagging for some requests.
Leo T: Searching logs for mis-tagged requests — found entries where `customer_tier=dedicated` and `route=canary` for a small set. Possibly a policy evaluation bug. Example:```
2026-02-18T01:24:00.001Z INFO request_id=xyz customer=tenant-42 customer_tier=dedicated route=canary model=s-1.12-canary
```
Arjun K: That's bad. Can you trace policy decision for request xyz? Which router instance made decision?
Leo T: Router instance r-07-az1 selected canary. Looking at router logs, rule evaluation shows `region: us-east` fallback to canary due to missing tier tag in token. Token introspection timed out and defaulted route->canary.
Priya N: So two issues: (A) token introspection timeouts, (B) canary routing default on missing tag. We should fix (B) to default to stable, not canary.
Maya S: Immediate mitigation: 1) Re-enable token-introspection cache to prevent timeouts 2) Patch router default rule to prefer stable 3) Roll back canary image to s-1.11 for safety if any leakage continues
Arjun K: I'm doing immediate router patch to change default route to stable. Will also re-enable introspection cache.
deploy-bot: Router config change applied by arjunk — default routing now stable -> effective 20s.
Rachel (ops): Monitoring shows dedicated requests to canary drop to near 0. Failed requests trending down as well. Good.
Leo T: For RCA we need: logs, exact list of tenants affected, configuration diffs, and canary image artifact hash. I pushed a timeline doc to the incident board: https://incidents/board/INC-2026-044/timeline
Priya N: Repro attempt: I spun a local instance with s-1.12-canary, ran parity tests hitting tokenizer heavily and saw intermittent `ValueError: Invalid token indices` at high concurrency. Attaching truncated trace:```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/decoder.py", line 214, in decode_chunk
    tokens = tokenizer.decode_batch(...)
ValueError: Invalid token indices
```
Arjun K: Given this and the packaging diff, decision: roll back canary image and pin router default to stable. Also open model-onboarding ticket to revert sentencepiece bump.
Maya S: I'll coordinate rollback. Rolling image tag s-1.12-canary -> s-1.11 now across canary cluster.
deploy-bot: Rollback job started by mayas — batch 1/6 canary nodes, batch 2 finishing. Logs:```
[rollback] node canary-03: pull s-1.11: sha256:abcd1234... OK
[rollback] node canary-03: drain connections -> success
```
Rachel (ops): Customer comms: CS notified, we sent an interim note to affected tenants; drafting post-incident update.
oncall-sre: Quick handoff: I'm taking over monitoring for the next hour while Arjun/Maya finalize RCA. Please DM if any regression.
Arjun K: Thanks — will add hypothesis tracker to the incident board and include action items: revert sentencepiece, add router unit test for missing-tier-case, ensure token introspection has cache and higher timeout, add canary isolation test in CI.
Priya N: Forensics: artifact hashes — canary s-1.12-canary sha256:aaaa1111, stable s-1.11 sha256:abcd1234. I'll attach to ticket.
Leo T: Next steps for postmortem: collect exact request ids of leaked dedicated requests, timestamped routing decisions, and root cause: misconfigured router default + tokenizer regression in upgraded sentencepiece.
Maya S: Closing immediate mitigation — canary traffic 0 and rollback complete 6m after alert. Marking incident as mitigated.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-044 status -> MITIGATED by oncall at 1769923765. Please complete postmortem template within 72h. :white_check_mark:
